assumedContext: Network egress blocked except the search index; the exact preferred balance, the exact share count and three peers' P/NAV readings could not be retrieved.

No fcf scenarios are supplied and weights.dcf is set to 0 deliberately: the asset produces no cash flow in any scenario, free cash flow to the firm is about -$1.6bn a year even in the bull case, and the common pays no dividend, so both an EV/FCF DCF and a dividend-discount model are undefined rather than merely difficult.

The book (P/B vs normalised ROE) method is omitted for the same reason: book value is NAV because the asset is marked to market under ASU 2023-08, so the justified-P/B formula collapses into a circular restatement of the P/NAV question.

The assetBase multiple supplied compounds two effects - the bitcoin price move and the P/NAV rating - so the workspace reproduces the same per-share answers from one gross-asset input. Implied bitcoin prices are $45,000 at 0.80x P/NAV (bear), $85,000 at 1.00x (base) and $150,000 at 1.25x (bull).

conclusions: Triangulated fair value is $143.70 against $128.48, an 11.9% premium to the current price, weighting scenario-based P/NAV 55% and today's liquidation SOTP 45%.
Expected three-year IRR is 14.5% against an 18.0% cost of equity. Positive and fat-tailed but below the hurdle, and that gap decides the rating.

Strategy trades at a 5% premium to its treasury-peer median of 0.99x, not a discount, and the premium is fully explained by scale, liquidity and index membership. The unexplained residual is approximately zero.
No DCF and no justified-P/B is run, deliberately: the asset produces no cash flow in any scenario and book value is NAV, so both methods are undefined rather than merely difficult.

Dispersion runs $32 to $370 and is almost entirely a bitcoin view. This file has an edge on the wrapper - its cost, leverage and mechanics - and none on the asset, which is why SOTP at today's price carries 45% of the weight.

Rating HOLD: neither the broken company a 65% drawdown implies nor the cheap leveraged proxy a $224-252 consensus implies. A competently run, unbreakable, expensive wrapper trading at roughly its own liquidation value plus a small, fully explained premium.
thesisImpact: Phase 5 contradicts nothing in Phases 1-4; it prices them and reaches a conclusion neither headline narrative supports. The disciplined answer is that the vehicle is worth approximately what it trades at, with the buy condition (P/NAV below 0.80x with the structure intact) and the sell conditions (NAV consumption, not a wider discount) specified so the position can be monitored rather than re-argued.

memo.weighting: P/NAV (asset-base) 55%, SOTP at today's liquidation value 45%, DCF 0%, P/B-vs-ROE 0%. The two zero weights are deliberate: the asset produces no cash flow in any scenario and free cash flow to the firm is about -$1.6bn a year even in the bull case, so an EV/FCF DCF is undefined; and book value IS net asset value because bitcoin is marked to market under ASU 2023-08, so the justified-P/B formula is a circular restatement of the P/NAV question. SOTP carries 45% because it embeds no bitcoin forecast, and a bitcoin forecast is not an edge this file possesses. Triangulated fair value $143.70 against $128.48; expected three-year IRR 14.5% against an 18.0% cost of equity. The peer note in model.peers uses P/NAV in the pb field, because for mark-to-market treasury vehicles price-to-book and price-to-NAV are the same ratio.

nonConsensus.market: MSTR is 'the leveraged bitcoin proxy' - buy it when you want amplified beta.
nonConsensus.us: The amplification is 1.37x, not the 2-3x the market still prices, and it is rented rather than owned: it is paid for with a 3.44% annual fee on common NAV that rises as bitcoin falls - 2.51% of the bitcoin stack at $77,000, 4.29% at $45,000, 6.44% at $30,000.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 4 section 4.4 leverage derivation ($65.08bn of exposure over $47.48bn of NAV); Phase 2 section 2.2 procyclical carry curve; STRC rate history 9.00% to 12.00% in fourteen months with a one-way ratchet.

nonConsensus.market: mNAV has collapsed from 3.89x, therefore MSTR is cheap and the discount will close.
nonConsensus.us: At 1.04x, Strategy trades ABOVE the 0.99x median of its treasury peers and far above the structural analogue - listed closed-end funds holding liquid assets with a fee and no durable edge have historically traded at 0.85-0.95x. Semler is at 0.88x and Nakamoto at 0.70x today. Mean reversion points down, not up.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 5 section 5.1 peer table and the premium decomposition, which leaves an unexplained residual of approximately zero; Phase 4 on the permanence of the spot-ETF overlay.

nonConsensus.market: BTC Yield of +13.3% year to date shows the compounding machine is still working.
nonConsensus.us: BTC Yield measures bitcoin per share and rises whenever stock is issued above 1.0x mNAV, regardless of the bitcoin price and regardless of what the capital cost. Year to date bitcoin per share rose 13.3% while the bitcoin price fell 12%, leaving bitcoin VALUE per share approximately flat and the shares 65% below their high. With the ATM shut and dividends funded by bitcoin sales, the same metric now runs at roughly -2.5% a year.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 3 section 3.2; company BTC Yield disclosure at 2026-05-25; bitcoin at $87,515 on 2025-12-31 against ~$77,000 today; 52-week range $81.81-$365.21.

fears.text: The reverse flywheel has no internal exit. mNAV below 1.0 makes issuance dilutive, so the ATM shuts; bitcoin per share then falls as dividends are funded by sales; which removes the reason to pay a premium; which keeps mNAV below 1.0.
fears.why: The loop is self-reinforcing in both directions and the only thing that breaks it is an exogenous bitcoin rally. A company whose recovery condition is the outcome it is supposed to produce does not control its own future. The purchase pause from mid-June to 2026-08-31, during which holdings grew by 1,481 bitcoin against 81,676 in the prior quarter, is this mechanism on the record.

fears.text: The carry is procyclical and the ratchet is one-way. At $77,000 the cash bill is 2.51% of the stack; at $45,000 it is 4.29%; at $30,000 it is 6.44% - and in exactly those states STRC trades below $95 and the rate ratchets permanently higher, about $53m a year per trigger.
fears.why: The rate has already gone from 9.00% at listing in July 2025 to 12.00% in September 2026. The liability structure is engineered to tighten when the asset falls, which is the risk an investment committee should refuse to underwrite cheaply.

fears.text: The access monopoly is permanently gone. Spot bitcoin ETFs deliver the same exposure for roughly 0.20% - one twelfth of Strategy's carrying cost - with daily creation and redemption at NAV.
fears.why: Creation and redemption at NAV is precisely the mechanism that prevents a discount from persisting, and Strategy has none. Its premium was built when it was the only regulated way to hold bitcoin in a brokerage account. Any future premium must be earned by leverage and the issuance machine alone, both of which are cyclical. This is the one part of the bear case that no bitcoin rally repairs.

sellTriggers: Bitcoin per share declining for three consecutive quarters
Cumulative bitcoin sales above 25,000 BTC in any rolling twelve months (about 3% of the stack)
Bitcoin holdings lower year-on-year in any quarter
USD reserve below $1.0bn (under eight months of carry cover)
Senior claims above 45% of bitcoin market value, against 33% today
Any secured borrowing against the bitcoin, or an S&P downgrade below B-
